<div>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">PART&nbsp;I<a name="Parti_002059"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Item 1.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Business</i><a name="Item1_Business_002101"></a></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Overview<a name="Overview_002104"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Countrywide Financial Corporation (&#147;Countrywide&#148;) is a
holding company which, through its subsidiaries (collectively, the &#147;Company&#148;),
is engaged in mortgage lending and other real estate finance-related
businesses, including mortgage banking, banking and mortgage warehouse lending,
dealing in securities and insurance underwriting.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We manage our
business through five business segments&#151;Mortgage Banking, Banking, Capital
Markets, Insurance and Global Operations. We primarily conduct the following
operations in these segments:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Mortgage Banking</i>&#151;We originate, purchase,
sell and service non-commercial mortgage loans nationwide.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Banking</i>&#151;We take deposits and invest in
mortgage loans and home equity lines of credit, sourced primarily through our
mortgage banking operation as well as through purchases from non-affiliates. We
also provide short-term secured financing to mortgage lenders.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Capital Markets</i>&#151;We operate an
institutional broker-dealer that primarily specializes in trading and
underwriting mortgage-backed securities. We also trade derivative products and
U.S. Treasury securities, provide asset management services and originate for
sale loans secured by commercial real estate. Within this segment we also manage
the acquisition and disposition of mortgage loans on behalf of the Mortgage
Banking Segment.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Insurance</i>&#151;We offer property, casualty,
life and disability insurance as an underwriter and as an insurance agency. We
also provide reinsurance coverage to primary mortgage insurers.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Global Operations</i>&#151;We license proprietary
technology to mortgage lenders in the UK. We also perform certain of the
Company&#146;s administrative and loan servicing functions through our India
operations.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mortgage banking continues
to be our core business, generating 48% of our pre-tax earnings in 2006. Our
other segments generated the following percentages of our pre-tax earnings in
2006: Banking&#151;32%; Capital Markets&#151;13%; Insurance&#151;6%; and Global Operations&#151;1%.
We remain a real-estate lending-centered company and have built upon our
mortgage banking operations in recent years to capitalize on meaningful related
opportunities with the intent of stabilizing our consolidated earnings profile.
For financial information about our segments, see the <i>Management&#146;s
Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#151;Operating
Segment Results</i> section and Note 26&#151;<i>Segments and
Related Information</i> in the financial statement section of this
Report.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Available
Information<a name="AvailableInformation_002111"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have a Web site located
at www.countrywide.com on which we make our Annual Reports on Form&nbsp;10-K,
Quarterly Reports on Form&nbsp;10-Q, Current Reports on Form&nbsp;8-K and all
exhibits and amendments to these reports available, free of charge, as soon as
reasonably practicable after such material is electronically filed with, or
furnished to, the Securities and Exchange Commission. Our Corporate Governance
Guidelines, our Code of Business Ethics, the charters of the committees of our
Board of Directors and all amendments and updates to these documents are also
available on our Web site and printed copies are available upon request.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">1</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='1',FILE='C:\fc\58172955463_D11448_1781074\4926-1-da.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Feb 27 17:31 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loan Production<a name="LoanProduction_002112"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We produce residential and
commercial mortgage loans within the Mortgage Banking, Banking and Capital
Markets Segments. Nearly all of the mortgage loans that we produce in the
Mortgage Banking and Capital Markets Segments are sold into the secondary
mortgage market, primarily in the form of securities and to a lesser extent in
the form of loans. We generally perform the ongoing servicing functions related
to the residential mortgage loans that we produce. Loans produced in our
Banking Segment have generally been held for investment.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Types of Products<a name="TypesOfProducts_002113"></a></font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We originate and
purchase mortgage loans that generally fall into one of the following four
categories:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Prime Mortgage Loans</i>&#151;These are prime
credit quality first-lien mortgage loans secured by single-family residences.
References to loans secured by single-family residences in this document
include loans secured by one-to-four dwelling unit residential real estate.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Prime Home Equity Loans</i>&#151;These are prime
credit quality second-lien mortgage loans, including home equity lines of
credit, secured by single-family residences.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Non</i><i><font style="font-style:italic;">p</font>rime Mortgage Loans&#151;</i>These are
first- and second-lien mortgage loans secured by single-family residences, made
to individuals with credit profiles that do not qualify them for a prime loan.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Commercial Real Estate</i>  <i>Loans&#151;</i>These are prime credit quality
first-lien mortgage loans secured by commercial properties, such as apartment
buildings, retail properties, office buildings, industrial sites, hotels and
other commercial properties.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The majority of our loan production consists of Prime
Mortgage Loans. Prime Mortgage Loans include conventional mortgage loans, loans
insured by the Federal Housing Administration (&#147;FHA&#148;) and loans guaranteed by
the Veterans Administration (&#147;VA&#148;). A significant portion of the conventional
loans qualify for inclusion in guaranteed mortgage securities backed by Fannie
Mae or Freddie Mac (&#147;conforming loans&#148;). Some of the conventional loans we
produce either have an original loan amount in excess of the Fannie Mae and
Freddie Mac loan limit for single-family loans ($417,000 for 2007) or otherwise
do not meet Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac guidelines. Loans that do not meet Fannie
Mae or Freddie Mac guidelines are referred to as &#147;nonconforming loans.&#148; In
certain tables and elsewhere in this Report, FHA and VA loans may be referred
to as Government Loans.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Acquisitions from third
parties.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For additional loan
production statistics, see the section in this Report entitled <i>Business&#151;Loan Production Tables.</i></font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mortgage Banking
Segment<a name="MortgageBankingSegment_002431"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Mortgage Banking
Segment produces mortgage loans through a variety of channels on a national
scale. The mortgage loans we produce in this segment are generally sold into
the secondary mortgage market, primarily in the form of securities, and to a
lesser extent in the form of loans. We typically perform the ongoing servicing
functions related to the mortgage loans that we produce. We also provide
various loan closing services such as escrow, flood determinations and
appraisal. We group the activities of our Mortgage Banking Segment into three
business sectors&#151;Loan Production, Loan Servicing and Loan Closing Services.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loan Production</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We produce mortgage loans
through three production channels of Countrywide Home Loans (&#147;CHL&#148;)&#151;Retail
Channel (Consumer Markets and Full Spectrum Lending), Wholesale Lending Channel
and Correspondent Lending Channel. These loans are funded either through one of
these channels or through Countrywide Bank. Countrywide Bank funds loans for
both our Mortgage Banking and Banking Segments.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>For additional
production statistics, see the section in this Report entitled <i>Business&#151;Loan Production Tables</i>.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>$106.0
billion and $8.1 billion of these loans were funded by Countrywide Bank during
the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005, respectively.</p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Retail Channel</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The retail channels consist of the Consumer Markets
Division (&#147;CMD&#148;) and the Full Spectrum Lending Division (&#147;FSLD&#148;). CMD generally
originates prime loans through existing relationships with customers and
organizations that influence the placement of mortgage services, while the Full
Spectrum Lending Division focuses on new customer acquisitions through mass
media advertising. In addition, FSLD originates nonprime mortgage loans.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For 2006, Countrywide was
ranked by <i>Inside Mortgage Finance </i>as
the second largest retail lender, in terms of volume, among residential retail
mortgage lenders nationwide. (Reprinted
with the permission of Inside Mortgage Finance Inc. (&#147;IMF&#148;) Copyrighted. All
rights reserved by IMF.)</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Consumer Markets
Division</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">CMD originates mortgage loans through three business
groups: the Distributed Retail group, the Business-to-Consumer group and the Strategic
Business Alliances group.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Distributed Retail group is the branch network
which originates loans through relationships with consumers, builders,
Realtors&#174; and through joint ventures. As of December&nbsp;31, 2006, this group
consisted of 773 branch offices in 48 states and the District of Columbia,
including 62 dedicated joint venture branches. This group has a sales force of
6,602, which includes those dedicated to joint venture relationships. The
Distributed Retail group (including the joint venture relationships) originated
74% of CMD total volume for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Business-to-Consumer group primarily originates
mortgage loans directly from existing customers through the Internet and
through our call centers. The Business-to-Consumer group focuses on customer
retention through marketing and by providing our existing customers with an
efficient and convenient means to obtain financing for a new home or for refinancing
their existing mortgage or a home equity loan. As of December&nbsp;31, 2006,
the Business-to-Consumer group consisted of five call centers with a sales
staff of 985. This group accounted for 18% of CMD&#146;s total volume for the year
ended December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Strategic Business
Alliance group facilitates and manages the development of new sources of loans
through relationships with organizations that influence the placement of
mortgage services. This </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">4</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">group
focuses primarily on developing revenue-sharing arrangements such as joint
ventures, third party outsourcing, relocation lending, marketing service
agreements and brokered-in agreements. This group accounted for 8% (excluding
Distributed Retail volume from joint venture relationships) of CMD&#146;s total
volume for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Full Spectrum
Lending Division</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FSLD originates Nonprime and Prime Mortgage Loans with
the primary focus on refinance and home equity products. FSLD operates through
a network of 226&nbsp;retail branch offices located in 39&nbsp;states, as well
as 11 call centers. The branches and call centers of FSLD are supported by four
fulfillment centers for processing, underwriting and funding of these mortgage
loans.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FSLD&#146;s mortgage production
is generated primarily through customer retention efforts directed to
Countrywide&#146;s nonprime servicing portfolio and new customer acquisition through
direct mail, Internet, mass media and joint venture relationships. Of the 226
FSLD retail branch offices, 56 operate with a large network of sales associates
who are dedicated to the fulfillment of referrals of Nonprime Mortgage Loan
customers from Countrywide&#146;s Consumer Markets Division.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Wholesale Lending
Channel</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Wholesale Lending Channel (&#147;WLD&#148;) underwrites and
funds mortgage loans sourced by mortgage loan brokers and other financial
intermediaries. WLD sources loans through approximately 30,000 mortgage loan
brokers nationwide. WLD offers a wide variety of Prime and Nonprime Mortgage
Loans and Prime Home Equity Loan products. Business is solicited through a
sales force, the Internet and advertising.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2006, WLD operated 52 branch
offices and seven fulfillment centers in various parts of the United States.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For 2006, Countrywide was
ranked by <i>Inside Mortgage</i>  <i>Finance </i>as the largest wholesale
originator, in terms of volume, among residential wholesale mortgage lenders
nationwide. (Reprinted with the
permission of IMF Copyrighted. All rights reserved by IMF.)</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Correspondent
Lending Channel</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Correspondent Lending Channel (&#147;CLD&#148;) purchases
mortgage loans from other lenders, which include mortgage bankers, commercial
banks, savings and loan associations, home builders and credit unions. As of December&nbsp;31,
2006, this Channel had correspondent relationships with approximately 2,100
lenders, who are subject to initial and ongoing credit evaluation and
monitoring. CLD operates in all 50&nbsp;states.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For 2006, Countrywide was
ranked by <i>Inside Mortgage</i>  <i>Finance </i>as the largest correspondent
lender, in terms of volume, among residential correspondent mortgage lenders
nationwide. (Reprinted with the
permission of IMF Copyrighted. All rights reserved by IMF.)</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Countrywide Bank
Mortgage Banking Activities</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As well as funding loans
for its investment portfolio, Countrywide Bank funds loans that are originated
for sale by our Mortgage Banking Segment. Because this activity is a Mortgage
Banking activity, the mortgage loan production, the related balance sheet and
the income relating to the holding and sale of these loans is included in our
Mortgage Banking Segment. The funding of loans by Countrywide Bank for our
Mortgage Banking operations provides an efficient means of financing loans
during the period the loans are held for sale.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">5</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Affordable and
Multicultural Home Loan Programs</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Since 1992, we have adopted a variety of affordable
home loan initiatives designed to increase homeownership opportunities for
low-to moderate-income borrowers and those with diverse backgrounds. Our
long-time initiative, known as <i>We </i>House
America&#174;, supports affordable housing programs undertaken by Fannie Mae and
promoted by various government agencies, including the U.S. Department of
Housing and Urban Development (&#147;HUD&#148;).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have specifically designed<i> We</i>
House America&#174; loan programs to meet the needs of low-to moderate-income
borrowers and others with financial, employment or personal situations which
might prevent them from qualifying for traditional mortgages. These loan
programs enable such borrowers to qualify for a home loan by allowing, for
example, lower down payments, lower cash reserves, alternative income sources
and more flexible underwriting criteria than on a typical loan. The mortgage
loans we produce through <i>We </i>House
America&#174; are sold and serviced on a non-recourse basis, generally through
guarantee programs sponsored by Fannie Mae.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Through <i>We </i>House
America&#174;, we provide telephone-based counseling services and Internet-based
resources to educate prospective first-time minority and low-to moderate-income
homebuyers about the home loan process. <i>We </i>House
America&#174; also provides Spanish-speaking counselors and instructors, and
educational materials printed in other languages.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have made other
significant commitments to affordable lending and multicultural markets
initiatives designed to increase homeownership opportunities among minority and
immigrant communities. For example, we are approved to participate in more than
930 mortgage loan programs that assist borrowers with down payments and closing
costs, which are offered by state, county and city agencies, municipalities and
not-for-profit organizations. In early 2005, we extended our five-year <i>We </i>House America&#174; Campaign, with a goal of
originating $1.0 trillion in loans to targeted borrower populations by the end
of 2010. As of December&nbsp;31, 2006, we made loans to 4.2 million borrowers
and funded $668 billion (including Prime and Nonprime Mortgage Loans) toward
this goal.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loan Servicing</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">When we sell or securitize mortgage loans, we
generally retain the rights to service these loans. These are referred to as
mortgage servicing rights (&#147;MSRs&#148;). We may also retain financial interests when
we securitize mortgage loans. We include the value of these retained interests
on our balance sheet. The results of the Loan Servicing Sector income statement
includes the changes in value related to our MSRs and retained interests, as
well as the revenues and expenses arising from servicing the mortgage loans.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In servicing mortgage
loans, we collect and remit loan payments, respond to customer inquiries,
account for principal and interest, hold custodial (impound) funds for payment
of property taxes and insurance premiums, counsel delinquent mortgagors and
supervise foreclosures and property dispositions. We receive servicing fees and
other remuneration in return for performing these functions.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mortgage Servicing Rights, Retained Interests and the
Servicing Hedge</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our MSRs arise from contractual agreements between us
and investors (or their agents) in mortgage-backed securities and mortgage
loans. Although MSRs generally arise from the sale or securitization of
mortgage loans that we originate, we also occasionally purchase MSRs from
others. For a more complete description of MSRs, see Note 3&#151;<i>Loan Sales</i> in the financial statement section of this
Report.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">MSRs and retained
interests are generally subject to a loss in value when mortgage rates decline.
To moderate the effect on earnings caused by a rate-driven decline in value of
MSRs and retained interests, we maintain a portfolio of financial instruments,
primarily derivative contracts, which generally increase in value when interest
rates decline. This portfolio of financial instruments is referred to as the &#147;Servicing
</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">6</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Hedge.&#148;
See Note 4&#151;<i>Derivative Financial Instruments&#151;Risk Management
Activities Related to Mortgage Servicing Rights (MSRs) and Retained Interests</i>
in the financial statement section of this Report for a further discussion of
our Servicing Hedge.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loan Servicing
Operations<a name="LoanServicingOperations_002717"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The various functions
within our loan servicing operations are briefly described in the following
paragraphs. These operations are performed in eight primary locations using the
same systems and processes: two in California, three in Texas, one in Arizona
and two in India.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Customer Service</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Customer Service Call
Centers managed nearly 58 million contacts with customers in 2006. These
contacts were primarily handled through our customer service representatives,
automated phone system and Website (www.customers.countrywide.com). This
division also prints monthly statements and oversees outbound customer
correspondence.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Remittance Processing</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Remittance Processing
division processes all payments, loan payoffs and payoff demand statements.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Collections and Loss Mitigation</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Collections and Loss
Mitigation units work with delinquent borrowers to bring their mortgages back
to current status and avoid foreclosure if possible. These efforts are tailored
to the specific circumstances of a borrower and comply with the requirements of
the mortgage investor.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Investor Accounting</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Investor Accounting
department reconciles custodial accounts, processes investor remittances and
maintains accounting records on behalf of our mortgage investors, including
Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and the Government National Mortgage Association (&#147;Ginnie
Mae&#148;), as well as private investors.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Foreclosure and Bankruptcy</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Foreclosure and bankruptcy
are complex processes that are subject to federal and state laws and
regulations, as well as mortgage investor and insurer requirements. Our
workflow-based systems facilitate consistent and compliant processing of
defaulted mortgage loans, as well as an efficient flow of data between internal
and external business partners. We use our own companies in support of many of
our foreclosure and bankruptcy activities to minimize related costs and to
increase efficiency.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Related Services</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We perform several loan
servicing functions internally that other loan servicers commonly outsource to
third parties. Our integrated services include performing property tax payment
processing, property inspections, and insurance tracking and premium payment
processing. We believe the integration of these functions gives us a
competitive advantage by lowering overall servicing costs and enabling us to
provide a high level of service to our mortgage customers and mortgage
investors.</font></p>

 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">9</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='9',FILE='C:\fc\5822382316_D11448_1782982\4926-1-dc.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Feb 27 22:40 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Loan Closing Services Sector</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We provide loan closing
products and services such as credit reports, appraisals, property valuation
services and flood determinations through our LandSafe,&nbsp;Inc. group of
companies. We provide these services primarily to customers referred by our
loan production channels, but also to third parties.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Competition and Consolidation</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The mortgage lending industry is dominated by large,
sophisticated financial institutions. To continue to compete effectively, we
will be required to maintain a high level of operational, technological, and
managerial expertise, as well as an ability to attract capital at a competitive
cost. Recently, well-capitalized Wall Street investment banking firms have
increased their participation in the mortgage banking business. We expect the
entrance of these firms to the marketplace to increase competition in the
near-term, especially in the nonconforming and nonprime loan products.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The industry continues to
undergo consolidation. We expect this trend to continue. We believe that we
will benefit from industry consolidation through increased market share and
enhanced ability to recruit talented personnel.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Banking Segment<a name="BankingSegment_234627"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Banking Segment
consists of the following operations:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The
investment and fee-based activities of <i>Countrywide
Bank, N.A.</i>, an FDIC-insured, federally-chartered bank (&#147;Banking
Operations&#148;)</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Countrywide Warehouse Lending</i>, a non-depository lending
company that provides short-term secured financing to mortgage lenders.</p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Countrywide Bank</font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:normal;">Banking Operations</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Banking Operations primarily fund and purchase
mortgage loans and home equity loans for investment purposes. The majority of
these loans are sourced through our Mortgage Banking production channels. For
liquidity and asset-liability management purposes, we also invest in securities
such as collateralized mortgage obligations and agency Mortgage-Backed
Securities (&#147;MBS&#148;). The Bank activities provide the Company with an expanded
product menu, lower cost funding sources and opportunities for a stable source
of revenue in the form of net interest income.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Banking Operations continue to leverage the
relationship with our Mortgage Banking Segment, sourcing high-quality mortgage
assets for our investment portfolio through the Mortgage Banking Segment&#146;s
existing production distribution channels, as well as through purchases of
loans from non-affiliated lenders. Asset growth is funded by the Bank&#146;s liability
base. The Bank obtains retail deposits, primarily certificates of deposit,
through 99 financial centers, 78 of which are located in CHL&#146;s retail branch
offices as of December&nbsp;31, 2006, call centers and the Internet. Countrywide
Bank also offers deposit accounts through deposit brokers (generally,
well-recognized financial intermediaries).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A significant portion of Countrywide Bank&#146;s deposit
liabilities are comprised of custodial funds that relate to the loan servicing
portfolio of CHL. Countrywide Bank also borrows funds from other sources to
supplement its deposit liabilities, including mortgage loan-secured borrowings
from the Federal Home Loan Bank (&#147;FHLB&#148;) of Atlanta, repurchase agreements
secured by purchased federal funds. Countrywide Bank also offers commercial
deposit accounts to title and mortgage insurance companies through a developing
commercial business unit.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">10</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='10',FILE='C:\fc\5822382316_D11448_1782982\4926-1-dc.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Feb 27 22:40 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Countrywide Bank acts as a mortgage document
custodian, primarily for our mortgage banking operations. As a document
custodian, we verify, maintain and release collateral for issuers, servicers,
sellers and purchasers of debt securitizations. We also provide other services,
including safekeeping, collateral review/certification, collateral releases and
customer reporting.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Properties
securing the mortgage loans in our Banking Operations&#146; portfolio of loans held
for investment are concentrated in the State of California. The following is a
summary of the geographical distribution of loans included in the Bank&#146;s loan
portfolio for the states with more than five percent of the total unpaid
principal balance at December&nbsp;31, 2006:</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mortgage Banking Activities</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Countrywide Bank produces
loans for sale which we have defined as a Mortgage Banking activity. The
mortgage loan production, the related balance sheet and the income relating to
the holding and sale of these loans is therefore included in our Mortgage
Banking Segment. We fund loans through Countrywide Bank for sale by our
Mortgage Banking Segment as an efficient means of financing loans during the
period the loans are held for sale.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Countrywide Warehouse Lending</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We provide committed and
uncommitted lines of credit to mortgage bankers to finance their mortgage loan
inventories, which we refer to as warehouse lending, through both a
non-depository lending company and Countrywide Bank. Most of these mortgage
bankers sell loans to our Mortgage Banking Segment&#146;s Correspondent Lending
Channel. All of these advances are secured by mortgage loans that have a market
value in excess of the balance of our advances.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Competition</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We operate in a highly competitive environment.
Competition for retail deposits comes primarily from other insured depository
institutions, which include more than 7,400&nbsp;commercial banks and
approximately 1,300&nbsp;savings institutions. We attract and retain deposits
through a combination of competitive rates, physical presence, experienced
banking professionals and easy access to our products through call centers and
the Internet at www.countrywidebank.com. Because of our low-cost structure
relative to other financial institutions, we are able to offer deposit rates
that are among the most competitive in the industry.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Countrywide Bank invests primarily in adjustable-rate
and short duration residential mortgage loans. Competition in making real
estate loans comes principally from other savings institutions, mortgage
banking companies and commercial banks. The majority of loans that the Banking
Segment invests in are sourced by the Mortgage Banking Segment. Countrywide
Bank also competes with commercial banks and investment banks in the purchase
of loans from third parties.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">11</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='11',FILE='C:\fc\5822382316_D11448_1782982\4926-1-dc.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Feb 27 22:40 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Banking Segment&#146;s
competitive position is enhanced by its relationship with our Mortgage Banking
Segment. For example, a significant portion of Countrywide Bank&#146;s deposit
liabilities consists of custodial funds controlled by CHL. As discussed above,
Countrywide Bank obtains retail deposit products through financial centers
placed within certain of CHL&#146;s retail branch offices. This economical use of
space reduces the Bank&#146;s deposit acquisition costs.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Capital Markets
Segment<a name="CapitalMarketsSegment_235030"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Capital Markets Segment primarily operates as a
registered securities broker-dealer, which is also a primary dealer of U.S.
Treasury securities, a residential mortgage loan manager and a commercial
mortgage loan originator. We also operate broker-dealers in Japan, Hong Kong
and the United Kingdom; an introducing broker of futures contracts; an asset
manager; a broker of MSRs and a derivatives dealer. With the exception of our
commercial mortgage activities, we transact primarily with institutional
customers, such as banks, other depository institutions, insurance companies,
asset managers, mutual funds, pension plans, other broker-dealers and governmental
agencies. Customers of our commercial real estate finance business are the
owners or sponsors of commercial properties, who can be individuals or
institutions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our activities consist of
the following:</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Conduit</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Conduit activities include
the purchase, warehousing and ultimate disposition of residential mortgage
loans on behalf of CHL. In our conduits, we manage both Nonprime Mortgage Loans
and Prime Mortgage Loans which are either acquired from third parties or
originated by CHL. We accumulate these loans for sale either through
securitizations or loan sales. We also manage the acquisition and disposition
of delinquent or otherwise illiquid residential mortgage loans, some of which
have been originated under FHA and VA programs. We attempt to cure the loans,
using the servicing operations of CHL, with the intent to securitize those
loans that become eligible for securitization. The remaining loans are serviced
through foreclosure and liquidation, which includes the collection of
government insurance and guarantee proceeds relating to defaulted FHA and VA
program loans.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Underwriting</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Capital Markets
participates in both competitive bid and negotiated underwritings and
underwrites for both CHL and third parties. Underwriting activities may encompass
the assumption of the market risk of buying a new issue of securities from the
issuer and reselling the securities to investors, either directly or through
dealers. Capital Markets primarily underwrites mortgage-related debt
securities. Capital Markets earns an underwriting spread that is the difference
between the amount paid to the issuer of securities and the offering price to
investors, net of expenses. The spread earned on each transaction and the level
of market risk assumed may vary based upon the nature of the market and the
terms of the underwriting agreement.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Securities Trading</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Securities trading
activities include the trading of debt securities in the secondary market after
the original issuance of the security and, to a much lesser extent, trading of
derivative financial instruments. We generally trade mortgage-related
fixed-income securities, including MBS, collateralized mortgage obligations and
asset-backed securities (&#147;ABS&#148;) issued by Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, Ginnie Mae
and other financial institutions, including CHL. We also trade securities
issued by the U.S. Department of Treasury and other governmental agencies.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">12</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='12',FILE='C:\fc\5822382316_D11448_1782982\4926-1-dc.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Feb 27 22:40 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Origination and Sale of Commercial Mortgage Loans</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Capital Markets originates
and sells commercial mortgage loans. Commercial mortgages are mortgages secured
by commercial properties, such as apartment buildings, retail properties,
office buildings, industrial sites and hotels.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Brokering</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Brokering activities
include brokerage of residential mortgage loan transactions, brokerage of MSRs,
brokerage of exchange-traded future contracts, advisory services and brokering
of exchange traded futures contracts and commodity options in an agent
capacity. The brokerage of residential mortgage loans, MSRs and futures
contracts may be between third parties or between CHL and third parties.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Asset Management</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Asset management
activities are conducted for the benefit of investors. This includes managing a
private equity fund, as well as management of collateralized debt and bond
obligations. We receive fees, including performance fees, for providing these
services. We may also share in the results of the funds when we hold an
investment interest in the fund.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Competition</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The securities industry is both highly competitive and
fragmented. In the mortgage securities market, we compete with global
investment banks as well as regional broker-dealers. We believe by leveraging
the strengths of CHL and by specializing in the mortgage securities market, we
can offer information, products and services tailored to the unique needs of
institutional customers, giving us an advantage in the market. In contrast, many
of our competitors offer a broader range of products and services, which may
place us at a competitive disadvantage. However, we believe that our
competitive position is strengthened by our offerings of more non-residential
mortgage related products and services to the global institutional investor
markets.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For 2006, according to <i>Inside MBS&nbsp;&amp; ABS,</i> we ranked
second among Non-Agency MBS Underwriters.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Insurance Segment<a name="InsuranceSegment_235139"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Insurance
Segment&#146;s primary activities are:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Offering
property, casualty, life and disability insurance as an underwriter and as an
insurance agent, offering warranty products and services, insurance tracking
services affiliated with our lender-placed insurance programs and an array of
commercial insurance products through our agency (&#147;Insurance Operations&#148;).</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Providing
reinsurance coverage to primary mortgage insurers (&#147;Reinsurance Operations&#148;).</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We manage these activities
through two business units&#151;Balboa Insurance Group and Balboa Reinsurance
Company.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Insurance Operations</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our insurance operations include our insurance
underwriters/carriers and their affiliated businesses, and our agency
operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We underwrite property, casualty, life and disability
insurance in 50 states and the District of Columbia through the insurers that
make up Balboa Insurance Group. Our retail insurance products are offered by
select general insurance agents serving the consumer market, including our
insurance agency.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">13</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='13',FILE='C:\fc\5822382316_D11448_1782982\4926-1-dc.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Feb 27 22:40 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our insurance
operations offer the following insurance product lines:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Lender-Placed Property and Automobile</i>&#151;We
offer lender-placed real-property hazard insurance and lender-placed automobile
insurance. Such insurance is provided on behalf of mortgage and automobile
lenders when borrowers fail to have agreed-upon insurance coverage in place to
protect the lender&#146;s security interest. We also provide insurance tracking
services, which alert a lender when there is a lapse in a borrower&#146;s insurance,
for more than 18.5 million loans, including nearly 8.2&nbsp;million loans
serviced within our Mortgage Banking Segment.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Voluntary Homeowners and Automobile</i>&#151;We
underwrite retail homeowners and automobile insurance for consumers under the
brand name Countrywide Insurance Group. We also offer home warranties to
consumers.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Life, Disability and Credit</i>&#151;We underwrite
term life, credit disability and credit life insurance products. Our retail
insurance products are offered by select general insurance agents servicing the
consumer market, including our affiliated agency.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2005, we filed a notice with the Florida Office
of Insurance Regulation to discontinue underwriting voluntary homeowners and
renters insurance in Florida. In March&nbsp;2006, the Florida office of
Insurance Regulation approved our plan to discontinue underwriting voluntary
homeowners and renters insurance in Florida, with non-renewal of residential
policies beginning July&nbsp;1, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Insurance Operations&#146; property and casualty
division has received an &#147;A (Excellent)&#148; rating from&nbsp;A.M. Best Company, an
insurance company rating and information service. Our life insurance operations
maintain an &#147;A- (Excellent)&#148; rating from&nbsp;A.M. Best Company. The &#147;Excellent&#148;
rating is defined by the&nbsp;A.M. Best Company as having &#147;an excellent ability
to meet ongoing obligations to policy holders.&#148;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our insurance agencies
provide consumers, in particular our mortgage customers, with homeowners, life,
disability, automobile and various other insurance products. Our insurance
agencies also operate a full-service commercial insurance program that offers a
comprehensive menu of products and services to meet the insurance needs of
small, mid-size and large businesses. The commercial insurance group
distributes a wide array of competitively priced property&nbsp;&amp; casualty
and employee benefits programs in specialty niche markets, including home
builders, mortgage brokers and bankers, real estate brokers and commercial
property owners.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Reinsurance Operations</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We provide mortgage
reinsurance to the insurance companies that provide primary mortgage insurance
(&#147;PMI&#148;) on loans in our servicing portfolio. This reinsurance covers losses in
excess of a specified percentage of the principal balance of a given pool of
mortgage loans, subject to a contractual limit, in exchange for a portion of
the pools&#146; mortgage insurance premium. We provide this coverage with respect to
substantially all of the loans in our portfolio that are covered by PMI, which
generally includes all conventional loans with an original loan amount in
excess of 80% of the property&#146;s appraised value. In return for providing this
coverage, we earn a portion of the PMI premiums.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Competition</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The lender-placed insurance market is dominated by a
small number of providers, competing on policy terms and conditions, service,
technological innovation, compliance capability, loan tracking ability and
price.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">14</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The homeowners, automobile, term life, credit-life and
credit-disability marketplaces are dominated by large, well-known providers.
Consumers select such insurance based on price, service and the efficiency and
effectiveness of marketing and underwriting operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We compete generally by
providing high-quality service and pricing our products at competitive rates,
as well as by leveraging our residential mortgage loan customer base.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Global Operations
Segment<a name="GlobalOperationsSegment_235300"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The primary
activities we conduct in our Global Operations Segment include:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Loan Processing and Subservicing&#151;</i>We
provided mortgage loan application processing and mortgage loan subservicing in
the UK until July&nbsp;31, 2006, when we discontinued such businesses. However,
we continue to license certain of the related technology to mortgage lenders in
the UK.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Offshore Services&#151;</i>We perform business process and technology
services for various units of the Company at three locations in India.</p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Competition</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our competitors in this
segment include business process outsourcers and technology companies operating
in Europe and India. We compete by leveraging Countrywide&#146;s mortgage expertise
and our proprietary technology.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financing of
Operations<a name="FinancingOfOperations_235329"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Uses of Financing</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have significant
financing needs. Our short-term financing needs arise primarily from the
following:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Warehousing
of mortgage loans pending sale</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Trading
activities of our broker-dealer</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Providing
mortgage warehouse credit to others.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our long-term
financing needs arise primarily from the following:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Investments
in mortgage loans</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Investments
in MSRs and interests that we retain when we securitize mortgage loans</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Financial instruments
acquired to manage the interest rate risk associated with those investments.</p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Sources of Financing</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We meet our
financing needs primarily through the following means:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Unsecured
commercial paper and medium-term notes</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Asset-backed

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Revolving

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Short-term

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font>&#160; Deposit-gathering</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>FHLB

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Unsecured
subordinated debt and junior subordinated debt, which includes high equity
content debt securities</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Retained
earnings.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We typically access the public corporate debt market
by issuing unsecured commercial paper, asset-backed commercial paper and unsecured
medium-term notes. At times, we may also issue subordinated debt, convertible
debt and securities that rating agencies credit with high equity content.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our
ongoing access to the public debt markets is dependent on a high credit rating.
For the last 14&nbsp;years, we have consistently maintained solid
investment-grade ratings. To maintain investment-grade ratings we must, among
other considerations, maintain a high level of liquidity, including access to
alternative sources of funding such as committed bank standby lines of credit.
We also must maintain a conservative debt-to-equity ratio. Current credit
ratings are as follows:</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We use short-term secured financing such as
asset-backed commercial paper conduits and repurchase agreements to finance a
substantial portion of our mortgage loan inventory and securities trading
portfolio. Countrywide Bank finances its investments in mortgage loans
primarily with a combination of deposit liabilities and secured FHLB advances.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We rely substantially on the secondary mortgage market
as a source of long-term capital to support our mortgage banking operations.
Most of the mortgage loans that we produce in our Mortgage Banking Segment and
Capital Markets Segment are sold in the secondary mortgage market, primarily in
the form of MBS and ABS.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our strategy is to ensure our ongoing access to the
secondary mortgage market by consistently producing quality mortgages and
servicing those mortgages at levels that meet or exceed secondary mortgage
market standards. We make significant investments in personnel and technology
to ensure the quality of our mortgage loan production.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our primary source of equity capital is retained
earnings. We supplement our equity capital with subordinated and junior
subordinated debt that receives varying degrees of &#147;equity treatment&#148; from
rating agencies, bank lenders and regulators. From time to time, we may issue
common stock or other debt securities that receive high equity treatment as a
means of supplementing our capital base and supporting our growth. We may also
repurchase common stock pursuant to the repurchase program approved by our
Board of Directors.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For a further discussion
of our liquidity and capital management see the section in this Report entitled
<i>Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial
Condition and Results of Operations&#151;Liquidity and Capital Resources.</i></font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest Rate Risk</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We typically bear interest
rate risk from the time we commit to make a loan at a specified interest rate
through the sale or repayment of the loan. We also bear interest rate risk
related to the interests we retain in the loans we sell, which are typically in
the form of MSRs and retained securities, and to the extent that our loan and
securities investment portfolios&#146; yields change on a different basis or at
different times than </font></p>
