<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company incurred
credit losses of $186.4 million, $124.0 million and $99.4 million related to
the Prime Home Equity and Nonprime Mortgage Loans with retained credit risk
during the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, 2005 and 2004, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Note 4&#151;Derivative
Financial Instruments<a name="Note4derivativeFinancialInstrumen_031614"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Derivative Financial Instruments</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The primary market risk facing the Company is interest
rate risk, which includes the risk that changes in market interest rates will
result in unfavorable changes in the value of our assets or liabilities (&#147;price
risk&#148;) and the risk that net interest income from our mortgage loan and
investment portfolios will change in response to changes in interest rates. The
overall objective of the Company&#146;s interest rate risk management activities is
to reduce the variability of earnings caused by changes in interest rates.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company manages interest rate risk in its Mortgage
Banking Segment through the natural counterbalance of its loan production and
servicing businesses. The Company also use various financial instruments,
including derivatives, to manage the interest rate risk related specifically to
the values of its commitments to make loans, (also referred to as interest rate
lock commitments or &#147;IRLCs&#148;), mortgage loans held by the Company pending sale (&#147;Mortgage
Loan Inventory&#148;), retained interests and trading securities, as well as a
portion of its debt.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company manages
interest rate risk in its Banking Segment by funding the segment&#146;s
interest-earning assets with liabilities of similar duration or a combination
of derivative instruments and certain liabilities that create repricing
characteristics that closely reflect the repricing behaviors of those assets.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Risk Management Activities Related to Mortgage Loan
Inventory and Interest Rate Lock Commitments</font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Description of Risk
Management Activities</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is exposed to price risk relative to its
Mortgage Loan Inventory and its IRLCs. The Mortgage Loan Inventory is comprised
of mortgage loans held by the Company pending sale, and is presently held for
an average of approximately 26 days. IRLCs guarantee the rate and points on the
underlying mortgage or group of mortgages for a specified period, generally
from seven to 75 days.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">With regard to loans held for sale, the Company is
exposed to price risk from the time an IRLC is made to a mortgage applicant or
financial intermediary to the time the resulting mortgage loan is sold. For
loans held for investment, the Company is exposed to price risk from the time
an IRLC is made to a financial intermediary to the time the loan is purchased.
During these periods, the Company is exposed to </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">24</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-24',FILE='C:\fc\58184916253_D11448_1781557\4926-1-fq.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Feb 27 18:50 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COUNTRYWIDE FINANCIAL CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS&#151;(Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">losses if mortgage rates
rise, because the value of the IRLC or mortgage loan held for sale declines. To
manage this price risk the Company uses derivatives.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The price risk management of IRLCs is complicated by
the fact that the ultimate percentage of applications that close within the
terms of the IRLC is variable. The probability that the loan will fund within
the terms of the IRLC is affected by a number of factors, in particular any
change in mortgage rates subsequent to the lock date. This probability
generally increases if mortgage rates rise, and decreases if mortgage rates
fall, due primarily to the relative attractiveness of current mortgage rates
compared to the applicant&#146;s committed rate. The probability that a loan will
fund within the terms of the IRLC is also influenced by the source and age of
the application, purpose for the loan (purchase or refinance), and the
application approval rate. The Company has developed closing ratio estimates,
using historical experience that take into account all of these variables, as
well as renegotiations of rate and point commitments that tend to occur when
mortgage rates fall. Those closing ratio estimates are used to estimate the
aggregate balance of loans that will fund within the terms of IRLCs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">To manage the price risk associated with the IRLCs,
the Company generally uses a combination of net forward sales of MBS and put
and call options on MBS, Treasury futures and Eurodollar futures. The Company
generally makes forward sales of MBS in an amount equal to the portion of the
IRLCs expected to close, assuming no change in mortgage rates. The Company
acquires put and call options to protect against the variability of loan
closings caused by changes in mortgage rates. To manage the credit spread risk
associated with its IRLC&#146;s the Company may enter into credit default swaps.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company manages the price risk related to the
Mortgage Loan Inventory primarily by entering into forward sales of MBS and
Eurodollar futures. The value of these forward MBS sales and Eurodollar futures
moves in opposite direction to the value of the Mortgage Loan Inventory. To
manage the credit spread risk associated with its Mortgage Loan Inventory, the
Company may enter into credit default swaps. The Company actively manages the
risk profiles of its IRLCs and Mortgage Loan Inventory on a daily basis.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company manages the price risk and credit risk
related to its commercial mortgage loans using interest rate swaps, total rate
of return and credit default swaps.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company uses
the following derivative instruments in its risk management activities related
to the IRLCs and Mortgage Loan Inventory:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Forward Sales of MBS:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; An obligation
to sell MBS at a specified price on a specified date in the future. The value
increases as mortgage rates rise.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Forward Purchases of MBS:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; An
obligation to buy MBS at a specified price on a specified date in the future. The
value increases as mortgage rates fall.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Long Call Options on MBS:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; A right to
buy MBS at a specified price on a specified date in the future. The value
increases as mortgage rates fall.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Long Put Options on MBS:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; A right to
sell MBS at a specified price on a specified date in the future. The value
increases as mortgage rates rise.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Long Call Options on U.S. Treasury Futures:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; A
right to acquire a U.S. Treasury futures contract at a specified price in the
future. The value increases as the benchmark U.S. Treasury rate falls.</p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">25</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-25',FILE='C:\fc\58184916253_D11448_1781557\4926-1-fq.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Feb 27 18:50 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COUNTRYWIDE FINANCIAL CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS&#151;(Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Long Put Options on U.S. Treasury Futures:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; A
right to sell a U.S. Treasury futures contract at a specified price on a
specified date in the future. The value increases as the benchmark U.S.
Treasury rate rises.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Short Eurodollar Futures Contracts</i>:&nbsp;&nbsp; A
standardized exchange-traded contract, the value of which is tied to spot
Eurodollar rates at specified future dates. The value increases when Eurodollar
rates rise.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Total Rate of Return Swaps:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; An agreement to pay or
receive the total return on a financial index or security in exchange for the
payment or receipt of a floating rate of interest over the term of the
contract. For use in the risk management of the commercial mortgage portfolio,
the Company pays the return on a published CMBS index and receives the floating
rate of interest. The value of these contracts increases as the value of the
index declines.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Credit Default Swaps:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; An agreement to purchase credit
event protection based on a financial index or security in exchange for paying
a fixed rate fee or premium over the term of the contract. For use in the risk
management primarily of commercial and residential mortgage loans, the Company
receives credit protection and pays a fixed fee or premium. The value of these
contracts increases when the probability of the occurrence of a credit event
rises.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Interest Rate Floors:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; Represents a
right to receive cash if a reference interest rate falls below a contractual
strike rate; therefore, its value increases as the reference interest falls. The
reference interest rates used in the Company&#146;s interest rate floors include
mortgage rates, Treasury rates and U.S. dollar (&#147;USD&#148;) LIBOR.</p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">26</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Accounting for Risk
Management Activities</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The change in value of all derivative instruments used
in the risk management activities related to Mortgage Loan Inventory and IRLCs
are recorded at fair value with changes in fair value included as a component
of gain on sale of loans and securities in the consolidated statement of
earnings.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">IRLCs that qualify as derivative instruments are
recorded at fair value with changes in fair value recognized in current period
earnings as a component of gain on sale of loans and securities. The IRLCs
related to loans held for sale and the IRLCs related to loans purchased for
investment generally qualify as derivative instruments.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company estimates the fair value of an IRLC based
on the change in estimated fair value of the underlying mortgage loan and the
probability that the mortgage loan will fund within the terms of the IRLC. The
change in fair value of the underlying mortgage loan is based upon quoted MBS
prices and is measured from the date the IRLC is issued. At the time of
issuance the estimated fair value of an IRLC is zero. Subsequent to issuance,
the value of an IRLC can be either positive or negative, depending on the
change in value of the underlying mortgage loan.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2006, the interest
rate risk management activities associated with 66% of the fixed-rate mortgage
loan inventory and 41% of the adjustable-rate mortgage loan inventory were
accounted for as fair value hedges. For the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2006,
2005 and 2004, the Company recognized pre-</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">27</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COUNTRYWIDE FINANCIAL CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS&#151;(Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">tax
losses of $116.9 million, $49.7 million and $116.2 million, respectively,
representing the ineffective portion of the hedges of its mortgage inventory
that qualified as fair value hedges under SFAS 133. These amounts are included
in gain on Sale of Loan and securities in the consolidated statements of
earnings.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Risk Management Activities Related to Mortgage
Servicing Rights and Retained Interests</font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Description of Risk
Management Activities</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">MSRs and retained interests, specifically interest-only
securities and residual securities, are generally subject to a loss in value
when mortgage interest rates decline. The fair value of MSRs and retained
interests are based on the present value of cash flow streams that are closely
linked to the expected life of the underlying loans. Declining mortgage
interest rates generally precipitate increased mortgage refinancing activity,
which decreases the expected life of the underlying loans, thereby decreasing
the value of the MSRs and retained interests. Changes in the value of these
assets are reflected in current period earnings for MSRs and retained interests
accounted for as trading securities. Impairment of retained interests accounted
for as available-for-sale securities is also reflected in current period
earnings; however appreciation in value above such interests&#146; amortized cost is
reflected as a component of other comprehensive income. To moderate any
negative impact on earnings caused by a rate-driven decline in fair value, the
Company maintains a portfolio of financial instruments, including derivatives,
which generally increase in aggregate value when interest rates decline. This
portfolio of financial instruments is collectively referred to herein as the &#147;Servicing
Hedge.&#148;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company uses the
following financial instruments in its Servicing Hedge:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Interest Rate Swaps:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; A mutual
agreement to exchange interest rate payments; one party paying a fixed rate and
another paying a floating rate tied to a reference interest rate (e.g., USD
LIBOR). For use in the Servicing Hedge, the Company generally receives the
fixed rate and pays the floating rate. Such contracts increase in value as
rates fall.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">Receiver Swaptions:</i><font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp; A right to enter into a predetermined
Interest Rate Swap at a future date where</font> the Company receives the fixed
rate and pays the floating rate. These contracts increase in value as rates
fall.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Payor Swaptions:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; A right to enter
into a predetermined Interest Rate Swap at a future date, where the Company
pays the fixed rate and receives the floating rate. These contracts increase in
value as rates rise.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Mortgage Forward Rate Agreement:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp;  A
mutual agreement to exchange a single cash flow at a forward settlement date,
based on the difference between the forward fixed rate and floating rate set
equal to the 30-day forward current coupon mortgage rate,&#160; known as the constant maturity index on the
settlement date. For use in the Servicing Hedge, the Company generally receives
the fixed rate and pays the floating rate. Such contracts increase in value as
the spread between the current coupon mortgage rate and the swap curve
tightens, or when interest rates fall.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Long Call Options on U.S. Treasury and Eurodollar
Futures:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; A right to acquire a U.S. Treasury or Eurodollar
futures contract at a specified price in the future. The value increases as the
benchmark U.S. Treasury or Eurodollar deposit rate falls.</p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">28</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-28',FILE='C:\fc\5517422490_D10695_1764246\4926-1-fs.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Feb 24 17:43 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COUNTRYWIDE FINANCIAL CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS&#151;(Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Long Put Options on U.S. Treasury and Eurodollar
Futures:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; A right to sell a U.S. Treasury or Eurodollar futures
contract at a specified price in the future. The value increases as the
benchmark U.S. Treasury or Eurodollar deposit rate rises.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Long U.S. Treasury Futures:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; An
agreement to purchase a U.S. Treasury security at a specified price in the
future. The value increases as the benchmark U.S. Treasury rate falls.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Interest Rate Caps:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; A right to receive cash if a
reference interest rate rises above a contractual strike rate. The value
increases as the reference interest rate rises. The reference interest rates
used in the Company&#146;s interest rate caps include mortgage rates, U.S. Treasury
rates, and USD LIBOR.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Interest Rate Floors:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; A right to
receive cash if a reference interest rate falls below a contractual strike rate.
The value increases as reference interest rates fall. The reference interest
rates used include mortgage rates, U.S. Treasury rates, and USD LIBOR.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">These instruments are combined to manage the overall
risk portfolio of the MSRs and retained interests. The Company actively manages
its retained interests risk profile on a daily basis.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
following table summarizes the activity for derivative contracts included in
the Servicing Hedge expressed by notional amounts:</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Servicing Hedge is
intended to reduce the impact on reported earnings of the decline in value of
MSRs and retained interests that generally results from a decline in mortgage
rates. Should mortgage rates increase, the value of the MSRs and retained
interests is expected to increase while the value of the Servicing Hedge is
expected to decrease.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Accounting for Risk
Management Activities</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The changes in fair value of derivative contracts
included in the Servicing Hedge are recorded as a component of the gain or loss
from the Servicing Hedge in the consolidated statements of earnings.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result of electing fair value accounting upon
adoption of SFAS 156 effective January&nbsp;1, 2006, the hedge provisions of SFAS
133 no longer apply to the risk management activities of the Company&#146;s MSRs.
Effective April&nbsp;1, 2005, a portion of the Servicing Hedge qualified as a
fair value hedge under SFAS 133. During the nine months ended December&nbsp;31,
2005, the portion of the Servicing Hedge that qualified as a fair value hedge
covered approximately 28% of the risk associated with a change in fair value of
the MSRs attributable to changes in interest rates of up to 50 basis points. At
no other time during the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2005 and 2004, did any
portion of the Servicing Hedge qualify as a hedge under SFAS 133. </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">29</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-29',FILE='C:\fc\5517422490_D10695_1764246\4926-1-fs.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Feb 24 17:43 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COUNTRYWIDE FINANCIAL CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS&#151;(Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the nine months ended December&nbsp;31,
2005, the Company recognized a loss of $29.3 million in earnings, which
represents the amount of hedge ineffectiveness for the portion of the Servicing
Hedge that qualified as a fair value hedge under SFAS 133.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There was no portion of the related hedge instruments&#146;
gain or loss that was excluded from the assessment of the hedge effectiveness.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Application of fair value
hedge accounting under SFAS 133 resulted in the cost basis of the MSRs being
adjusted for the change in fair value of the MSRs attributable to the hedged
risk, with a corresponding amount included as a component of impairment or
recovery of MSRs interests in the statement of earnings.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Risk Management Activities Related to Issuance of
Long-Term Debt</font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Description of Risk
Management Activities</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management&#146;s objective in financing the activities of
the Company is to ensure access to reliable and cost-effective funding from a
variety of sources in order to meet the Company&#146;s financing requirements under
various market conditions. These financing activities subject the Company to
interest rate risk. Specifically, the Company is exposed to the risk that the
interest expense it incurs on its long-term borrowings will change at a
different speed than the income it earns on the assets financed by the
long-term debt, contributing to variability of net income. To address this
risk, management seeks long-term debt structured to reprice in a manner similar
to the assets it is financing. However, the Company may not be able to obtain
access to borrowings structured to match the repricing characteristics of the
assets being financed at optimal interest rates (i.e., cost). Management
addresses this constraint, in part, by entering into interest rate and foreign
currency swap agreements designed to modify the structure of its borrowings. These
agreements have the effect of changing the structure of a debt agreement to one
that approximates the repricing characteristics of the assets financed.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has entered into interest rate swap
contracts swaps in which the rate received is fixed and the rate paid is
adjustable and is indexed to LIBOR (&#147;Receiver Swap&#148;). These interest rate swaps
enable the Company to convert a portion of its fixed-rate, long-term debt to
U.S. dollar LIBOR-based floating-rate debt (notional amount of $5.5 billion as
of December&nbsp;31, 2006) and a portion of its foreign currency-denominated
fixed and floating-rate, long-term debt to U.S. dollar LIBOR-based
floating-rate debt (notional amount of $4.5 billion as of December&nbsp;31,
2006). These transactions are generally designated as fair value hedges under
SFAS&nbsp;133.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
following summarizes the notional amounts and the average interest rates of the
swaps as of December&nbsp;31, 2006:</font></p>

<div align="center">

<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse;">

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Payments on interest rate
swaps are based on a specified notional amount and payments are due
periodically through the termination date of each contract. The swap contracts
expire between February&nbsp;2007 and November&nbsp;2036.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">30</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-30',FILE='C:\fc\5517422490_D10695_1764246\4926-1-fs.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Feb 24 17:43 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COUNTRYWIDE FINANCIAL CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS&#151;(Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Accounting for Risk
Management Activities</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The interest rate swaps are recognized on the balance sheet
at fair value.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, 2005 and
2004, the Company recognized a pre-tax gain of $23.3 million, a pre-tax loss of
$2.1 million, and a pre-tax loss of $3.8 million, respectively, representing
the ineffective portion of its fair value hedges of debt. These amounts are
included in interest expense in the consolidated statements of earnings.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2006, 2005 and 2004, the Company recognized no pre-tax gain or loss, a pre-tax
gain of $0.5 million, and a pre-tax gain of $0.04 million, respectively,
representing the ineffective portion of such cash flow hedges. As of December&nbsp;31,
2006, deferred net gains or losses on derivative instruments included in
accumulated other comprehensive income that are expected to be reclassified as
earnings during the next twelve months are not material.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Risk Management Activities Related to Deposit
Liabilities</font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Description of Risk
Management Activities</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company faces interest rate risk in the
interest-earning activities of its Bank. Specifically, the Company is exposed
to the risk that the interest expense it incurs on its deposits will change at
a different rate than the income it earns on its interest-earning assets,
resulting in variability in net interest income. Management manages this risk
by matching the duration and re-pricing characteristics of the Bank&#146;s
interest-bearing liabilities with those of its interest-earning assets. To
align the repricing characteristics of its interest-earning assets, the Company
enters into interest rate swap contracts that have the effect of converting a
portion of its fixed-rate deposit liabilities to LIBOR-based variable-rate
deposit liabilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
following summarizes the notional amounts and the average interest rates of the
swaps as of December&nbsp;31, 2006:</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Payments are due
periodically through the termination date of each swap contract. The contracts
expire between September&nbsp;2007 and November&nbsp;2026.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Accounting for Risk
Management Activities</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Bank&#146;s interest rate
swap transactions are designated as fair value hedges. For the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2006 and 2005, the Company recognized pre-tax losses of $1.6&nbsp;million and
$0.3 million, respectively, representing the ineffectiveness related to these
swaps. These amounts are included in interest expense in the consolidated
statement of earnings. For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2004, certain of
the swaps with a notional value totaling $752 million were accounted for as
free-standing derivatives, with changes in the swaps&#146; fair value and cash flow
from the swaps recorded in interest expense. Effective January&nbsp;1, 2005,
these swaps were designated and accounted for as fair value hedges of certain
fixed-rate deposits.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">31</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COUNTRYWIDE FINANCIAL CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS&#151;(Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Risk Management Activities Related to the
Broker-Dealer Securities Trading Portfolio</font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Description of Risk
Management Activities</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with
its broker-dealer activities, the Company maintains a trading portfolio of
fixed-income securities, primarily MBS. The Company is exposed to price changes
in its trading portfolio arising from interest rate changes during the period
it holds the securities. To manage this risk, the Company utilizes the
following derivative instruments:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Forward Sales of To-Be Announced (&#147;TBA&#148;) MBS:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; An
obligation to sell agency pass-through MBS that have not yet been issued on a
specified price and at a specified date in the future. The value increases as
mortgage rates rise.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Forward Purchases of TBA MBS:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; An
obligation to purchase at a specified price on a specified date in the future
agency pass-through MBS that have not yet been issued. The value increases as
mortgage rates fall.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Short Futures Contract:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; A
standardized exchange-traded contract, the value of which is tied to spot
Federal Funds or Eurodollar rates at specified future dates. The value of these
contracts increases when Federal Funds or Eurodollar rates rise.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Long Futures Contracts:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; A
standardized exchange-traded contract, the value of which is tied to the spot
Federal Funds or Eurodollar rates at specified future dates. The value of these
contracts increases when Federal Funds or Eurodollar rates fall.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Interest Rate Swaps:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; A mutual
agreement to exchange interest rate payments; one party paying a fixed rate and
another paying a floating rate tied to a reference interest rate (e.g., USD
LIBOR). For use in its trading portfolio risk management activities, the
Company receives the floating rate and pays the fixed rate. Such contracts
increase in value as rates rise.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Long Put Options on Federal Funds and Eurodollar
Futures:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; A right to sell Federal Funds or Eurodollar futures
contract at a specified price on a specified date in the future. The value
increases as the benchmark Federal Funds or Eurodollar rate rises.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Long Call Options on Federal Funds and Eurodollar
Futures:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; A right to acquire Federal Funds or Eurodollar
futures contract at a specified price on a specified date in the future. The
value increases as the benchmark Federal Funds or Eurodollar rate falls.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Interest Rate Caps:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; Represents a
contract that requires the issuer to make a payment to the holder when an
underlying interest rate exceeds a specified level. Interest rate caps increase
in value as interest rates rise.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Receiver Swaptions:</i>&nbsp;&nbsp; A right to enter
a predetermined Interest Rate Swap at a future date where we receive the fixed
rate and pay the floating rate. These contracts increase in value as rates
fall.</p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">32</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Accounting for Risk
Management Activities</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The changes in fair value
of derivative contracts used in the interest rate management activities related
to trading activities are recorded as a component of the gain on sale of loans
and securities in the consolidated statements of earnings.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Counterparty Credit Risk</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is exposed to credit loss in the event of
contractual non-performance by its trading counterparties and counterparties to
its various over-the-counter derivative financial instruments. The Company
manages this credit risk by selecting only counterparties that the Company
believes to be financially strong, spreading the credit risk among many such
counterparties, by placing contractual limits on the amount of unsecured credit
extended to any single counterparty and by entering into netting agreements
with the counterparties as appropriate.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
aggregate amount of counterparty credit exposure after consideration of
relevant netting agreements at December&nbsp;31, 2006, before and after
collateral held by the Company is as follows:</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2006, the Company had pledged
$7.9 billion and $0.6 billion in mortgage loans held for sale to secure
asset-backed commercial paper and a secured revolving line of credit,
respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2005,
the Company had pledged $13.0 billion and $3.0 billion in mortgage loans held
for sale to secure asset-backed commercial paper and a secured revolving line
of credit, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005, $19.5 billion
and $9.0 billion, respectively, of the Company&#146;s trading securities had been
pledged as collateral for financing purposes, of which the counterparty had the
contractual right to sell or re-pledge $1.5 billion and $0.7 billion,
respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2006, 2005 and 2004, the Company recorded $25.9 million in gains, $203.7
million in gains and $1.7 million in losses, respectively, on trading
securities that related to trading securities still held at the respective
period-end reporting dates.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">It is the policy of the Company to obtain possession
of collateral with a market value equal to or in excess of the principal amount
loaned under securities purchased under agreements to resell. Collateral is
valued daily, and the Company may require counterparties to deposit additional
collateral or may return collateral pledged when appropriate. Securities
borrowed transactions require the Company to deposit cash, letters of credit or
other collateral with the lender in an amount generally in excess of the market
value of the securities borrowed.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31,
2006 and 2005, the Company had accepted collateral related to securities
purchased under agreements to resell and securities borrowed with a fair value
of $56.0 billion and $33.7 billion, respectively, that it had the contractual
ability to sell or re-pledge, including $30.0 billion and $12.1 billion,
respectively, related to amounts offset by securities sold under agreements to
repurchase under master netting arrangements. As of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and
2005, the Company had re-pledged $52.1 billion and $28.3 billion, respectively,
of such collateral for financing purposes.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mortgage loans held for investment totaling $57.5
billion and $52.2 billion were pledged to secure Federal Home Loan Bank (&#147;FHLB&#148;)
advances and to enable additional borrowings from the FHLB at December&nbsp;31,
2006 and 2005, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mortgage loans held for investment totaling
$2.9&nbsp;billion and $2.0 billion were pledged to secure an unused borrowing
facility with the Federal Reserve Bank (&#147;FRB&#148;) at December&nbsp;31, 2006 and
2005, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company had accepted mortgage loan collateral of
$3.5 billion and $4.1 billion securing warehouse-lending advances that it had
the contractual ability to re-pledge as of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005,
respectively. Of this amount, $1.6 billion has been re-pledged to secure
borrowings under a secured revolving line of credit as of December&nbsp;31,
2006. No mortgage loan collateral was re-pledged as of December&nbsp;31, 2005.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has not
identified any individually evaluated loans as impaired as of December&nbsp;31,
2006 and 2005. The Company has placed loans on nonaccrual status totaling $2.1
billion and $1.4 billion at December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005, respectively.
Included in total nonaccrual loans were Government-insured or guaranteed loans
totaling $1.4 billion and $1.1 billion at December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005,
respectively. No warehouse lending loans were considered by management to be
impaired as of December&nbsp;31, 2006 or 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Changes
in the allowance for the loan losses were as follows:</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Concentrations of
Credit Risk</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company reviews its
portfolio of loans held for investment for concentrations of loans that might
contain disproportionate credit risk. Specifically, the Company&#146;s credit risk
management staff monitors loan performance by state and by Metropolitan
Statistical Area, as well as by product. Underwriting guidelines and investment
objectives are adjusted based on management&#146;s assessment of the results of
performance monitoring.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Although pay-option ARMs have decreased in prominence,
from approximately 19% of loan originations during the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2005, to approximately 14% during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, the
Company has retained a significant portion of its pay-option adjustable-rate (&#147;pay-option
ARM&#148;) loan production in its investment portfolio. Pay-option ARM loans
represent 46% and 41% of the Company&#146;s investment in mortgage loans held for
investment at December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005, respectively.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">37</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-37',FILE='C:\fc\58185125181_D11448_1781557\4926-1-fu.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Feb 27 18:52 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COUNTRYWIDE FINANCIAL CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS&#151;(Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pay-option ARM loans have
interest rates that adjust monthly and contain features that allow the borrower
to defer making the full interest payment for at least the first year of the
loan. After this &#147;option&#148; period, minimum monthly payments increase by no more
than 7&#189;% per year unless the unpaid balance increases to a specified limit,
which is no more than 115% of the original loan amount, at which time a new
monthly payment amount adequate to repay the loan over its remaining
contractual life is established. To ensure that contractual loan payments are
adequate to repay a loan, the fully amortizing loan payment amount is
re-established after either, five or ten years and again every five years
thereafter. Due to the lack of significant historical experience at
Countrywide, the credit performance of these loans has not been established for
the Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Due to pay-option ARM
loans&#146; amortization characteristics, the loss that the Company would realize in
the event of default may be higher than that realized on a &#147;traditional&#148; loan
that does not provide for deferral of a portion of the fully amortizing loan
payment. Countrywide&#146;s pay-option ARM loans are designed with features that
address the risk of borrower default and the increased risk of loss in the
event of default. Specifically, Countrywide&#146;s underwriting standards conform to
those required to make the pay-option ARM loans salable into the secondary
market at the date of funding, including a requirement that the borrower meet
secondary market debt-service ratio tests based on their making the fully
amortizing loan payment assuming the loan&#146;s interest rate is fully indexed. (A
fully indexed loan rate equals the sum of the current index rate plus the
margin applicable to the loan.) The loans&#146; terms limit the amount of potential
increase of loss in the event of default by restricting the amount of interest
that may be added to the loan&#146;s balance as described in the preceding
paragraph.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Following
is a summary of pay-option ARM loans held for investment:</font></p>

<div style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><hr size="1" width="160" noshade color="black" align="left" style="width:120.0pt;"></div>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.5pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The
ratio of the lower of the amount of the loan that is secured by the property to
the original appraised value or purchase price of the property.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.5pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The
ratio of the lower of the amount of all loans secured by the property to the original
appraised value or purchase price of the property.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(3)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>A FICO score is a measure
of borrower creditworthiness determined using a statistical model. FICO scores
range from approximately 300 to 850, with a higher score indicating an
individual with a more favorable credit profile.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management expects the delinquency rate in the Company&#146;s
pay-option ARM loan portfolio to increase as this product seasons.</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COUNTRYWIDE FINANCIAL CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS&#151;(Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005, the Company had
pledged $0.1 billion and $2.1 billion, respectively, of MBS to secure
securities sold under agreements to repurchase, which the counterparty had the
contractual right to re-pledge and $0.1 billion and $0.3 billion, respectively,
of MBS to secure an unused borrowing facility with the FRB.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s insurance subsidiaries have deposited
mortgage-backed securities with a fair value of $0.02 billion to meet state
statutory deposit requirements, at December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Amortized

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s Asset/Liability Committee (&#147;ALCO&#148;)
assesses securities classified as available-for-sale for other-than-temporary
impairment on a quarterly basis. This assessment evaluates whether the Company
intends and is able to recover the amortized cost of the securities when taking
into account the Company&#146;s present investment objectives and liquidity
requirements and whether the creditworthiness of the issuer calls the
realization of contractual cash flows into question. Based on the Company&#146;s
review of these securities, ALCO has concluded that Countrywide has both the
intent and ability to hold these securities until they recover their amortized
cost and the issuers credit worthiness does not call realization of contractual
cash flows into question. Accordingly, other-than-temporary impairment related
to these securities has not been recognized as of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and
2005.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Principally reflects
changes in discount rates and prepayment speed assumptions, primarily due to
changes in interest rates.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Represents changes due
to realization of expected cash flows.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The estimated fair values
of MSRs were $12.7 billion and $8.9 billion as of December&nbsp;31, 2005 and
2004, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company had pledged
$1.2 billion and $0.1 billion of securities broker-dealer receivables to secure
securities sold under agreements to repurchase at December&nbsp;31, 2006 and
2005, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company routinely enters short-term financing
arrangements to sell securities under agreements to repurchase (&#147;repurchase
agreements&#148;). The repurchase agreements are collateralized by mortgage loans
and securities. All securities underlying repurchase agreements are held in
safekeeping by broker-dealers or banks. All agreements are to repurchase the
same or substantially identical securities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Scheduled
maturities of securities sold under agreements to repurchase were as follows:</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><hr size="1" width="160" noshade color="black" align="left" style="width:120.0pt;"></div>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Averages represent daily
balance sheet estimates which do not reflect netting of securities under master
netting agreements.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2006, repurchase agreements were
secured by $19.5 billion of trading securities, $52.1 billion of securities
purchased under agreements to resell and securities borrowed, $0.1 billion in
investments in other financial instruments and $1.2 billion of other assets. At
December&nbsp;31, 2006, $30.0 billion of the pledged securities purchased under
agreements to resell and securities borrowed related to amounts were offset
against securities sold under agreements to repurchase pursuant to master
netting agreements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2005, repurchase agreements were
secured by $9.0 billion of trading securities, $28.3&nbsp;billion of securities
purchased under agreements to resell and securities borrowed, $2.1 billion in
investments in other financial instruments and $0.1 billion of other assets. At
December&nbsp;31, 2005, $12.1&nbsp;billion of the pledged securities purchased
under agreements to resell and securities borrowed related to amounts were
offset against securities sold under agreements to repurchase pursuant to
master netting agreements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Federal funds purchased generally represent overnight
borrowings of reserves from other banks in the Federal Reserve Bank System.
Interest is generally settled the next business day at the federal funds rate.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financial
data pertaining to federal funds purchased were as follows:</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Of the total advances, $17.9 billion were fixed-rate
and $10.3 billion were adjustable-rate.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2006
and 2005, the Company had pledged $57.5 billion and $52.2 billion of mortgage
loans to secure its outstanding FHLB advances and enable future advances,
respectively.</font></p>

(CFC) and Countrywide Home Loans (CHL) under various shelf registrations filed
with the Securities and Exchange Commission or issued by CFC and CHL under its
European and Australian medium-term note programs were as follows:</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, the
Company issued $6.6 billion and $0.6 billion of floating-rate and fixed-rate
medium-term notes, respectively. Of the $0.6 billion of fixed-rate medium-term </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">51</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-51',FILE='C:\fc\585153042_H10187_1775724\4926-1-ga.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Feb 27 05:17 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COUNTRYWIDE FINANCIAL CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS&#151;(Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">notes issued by the
Company during the year-ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, $0.5 billion were
effectively converted to floating-rate debt using interest rate swaps.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31,
2006, $4.5 billion of foreign currency-denominated medium-term notes were
outstanding. Such notes are denominated in Pounds Sterling, Canadian Dollars,
Australian Dollars, Euros, Swiss Francs and Singapore Dollars. These notes have
been effectively converted to U.S. dollars through currency swaps.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Asset-Backed Commercial Paper</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has formed two special purpose entities to
finance certain of its mortgage loans held for sale using commercial paper.
These entities issue commercial paper in the form of short-term secured
liquidity notes (&#147;SLNs&#148;) with initial maturities of up to 180 days. The SLNs
bear interest at prevailing money market rates approximating LIBOR. The SLN
programs&#146; capacities, based on aggregate commitments from underlying credit
enhancers, totaled $30.7 billion at December&nbsp;31, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financial
data pertaining to SLNs were as follows:</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Secured Revolving Lines of Credit</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2004, the Company formed a special purpose
entity for the purpose of financing inventory with funding provided by a group
of bank-sponsored conduits that are financed through the issuance of
asset-backed commercial paper. The entity incurs interest based on prevailing
money market rates </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">52</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COUNTRYWIDE FINANCIAL CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS&#151;(Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">approximating the cost of
asset-backed commercial paper. At December&nbsp;31, 2006, the entity had
aggregate commitments from the bank-sponsored conduits totaling $10.4&nbsp;billion
and had $0.6 billion outstanding borrowings, secured by $0.6 billion of
mortgage loans held for sale.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financial

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A new $4.0 billion master trust facility commenced on June&nbsp;2,
2006 to finance Countrywide Warehouse Lending (&#147;CWL&#148;) receivables backed by
mortgage loans. A multi-asset conduit finance company funds the purchase of
notes backed by CWL receivables which are financed by issuing extendable
maturity asset-backed commercial paper. The borrowing under this facility at December&nbsp;31,
2006, was $1.5 billion, and the Company had pledged $1.6 billion in loans held
for investment to secure this facility.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financial
data pertaining to the master trust facility secured revolving line of credit
were as follows:</font></p>

<div align="center">

<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse;">

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Asset-Backed Secured Financings</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company recorded
certain securitization transactions as secured borrowings as of December&nbsp;31,
2006 and 2005, because they did not qualify for sales treatment under SFAS 140.
The amounts accounted for as secured borrowings totaled $241.2 million and
$23.0 million at December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Junior Subordinated Debentures</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2006, the Company redeemed at par
plus accrued interest, the 8% Capital Securities of Countrywide Capital I (the &#147;Subsidiary
Trust I&#148;).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Countrywide Capital III (the &#147;Subsidiary Trust III&#148;),
a subsidiary trust of the Company, has $200 million outstanding of 8.05%
Subordinated Capital Income Securities, Series&nbsp;A (the &#147;8.05% Capital
Securities&#148;). In connection with the Subsidiary Trust III issuance of 8.05%
Capital Securities, CHL issued to the Subsidiary Trust III $206 million of its
8.05% Junior Subordinated Deferrable Interest Debentures (the &#147;Subordinated
Debt Securities III&#148;). The Subordinated Debt Securities III are due on June&nbsp;15,
2027 </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">53</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">
