<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COUNTRYWIDE FINANCIAL CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS&#151;(Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">FHA-Insured
and VA-Guaranteed Loans</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FHA-insured and
VA-guaranteed mortgage loans are generally pooled into MBS guaranteed by Ginnie
Mae. The Company is insured against foreclosure loss by the FHA or partially
guaranteed against foreclosure loss by the VA. Fees charged by the FHA and VA
for assuming such risks are paid directly by the borrower. The Company is
exposed to credit losses on defaulted VA loans to the extent that the partial
guarantee provided by the VA is inadequate to cover the total credit losses
incurred. The Company pays guarantee fees to Ginnie Mae for Ginnie Mae&#146;s
guarantee on its securities of timely payment of principal and interest. Ginnie
Mae does not assume mortgage credit risk associated with the loans securitized
under its program.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">Non-conforming
Conventional Loans</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Non-conforming conventional prime mortgage loans are
generally pooled into &#147;private-label&#148; (non-agency) MBS. Such securitizations
involve some form of credit enhancement such as senior/subordinated structures,
including residual interests, overcollateralization or mortgage pool insurance.
Securitizations that involve senior/subordinated structures contain securities
that assume varying levels of credit risk. Holders of subordinated securities
are compensated for the credit risk assumed through a higher yield. When we
sell the subordinated securities created in connection with these
securitizations we transfer the related credit risk subject to representations
and warranties we make when the loans are securitized.&#160; When we retain the subordinated securities,
generally the residual interests, we are in the first loss position; however,
the recourse for credit losses is limited to the carrying value of the residual
securities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In some cases a portion of the retained residual
interest is deposited into a net interest margin (&#147;NIM&#148;) security, which
enables us to sell some of the future residual cash flows and retain a smaller
residual interest (&#147;Back-end NIM Residual&#148;). The holder of the Back-end NIM
Residual is in the first loss position; however, the recourse for credit losses
is limited to the carrying value of the Back-end NIM residual.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">Prime
Home Equity Loans</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Prime Home Equity loans
are generally pooled into private-label asset-backed securities. The Company
generally securitizes these loans with limited recourse for credit losses
through retention of residual interests and other subordinated interests, such
as transferor&#146;s interests. The holder of the residual interest is in the first
loss position; however, the recourse for credit losses is limited to the
carrying value of the residual interest. These securities generally contain
credit enhancement in the form of over-collateralization and guarantees
provided by a third-party surety. In some cases, the securitizations also
contain mortgage pool insurance or a limited corporate guarantee as a form of
credit enhancement.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">Nonprime
Mortgage Loans</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Nonprime Mortgage Loans generally are pooled into
private-label asset-backed securities. The Company generally securitizes these
loans with limited recourse for credit losses through retention of residual
interests, the value of which ranges from 1.00% to 5.50% of the principal
balance of the loans. The holder of the residual interest is in the first loss
position; however, the recourse for credit losses is limited to the carrying value
of the residual interest. In some cases, such limited recourse securitizations
have contained lender paid mortgage insurance as a form of credit enhancement
or a limited corporate guarantee from Countrywide. The Company also has pooled
a portion of our Nonprime Mortgage Loans </font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-85</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-85',FILE='C:\fc\59162512693_D11448_1789751\4926-1-gm.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Feb 28 16:26 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COUNTRYWIDE FINANCIAL CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS&#151;(Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">into securities guaranteed
by Fannie Mae. In such cases, the Company has paid Fannie Mae a guarantee fee
in exchange for Fannie Mae assuming the credit risk of the underlying loans.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In some cases the retained residual interest is
deposited into a net interest margin security, which enables the Company to
sell future residual cash flows and retain a smaller residual interest (&#147;Back-end
NIM Residual&#146;&#146;). The value of the Back-end NIM Residuals range from 0.00% to
1.50%&nbsp;of the principal balance of the loans underlying the residual
security. The holder of the Back-end NIM Residual is in the first loss
position; however, the recourse for credit losses is limited to the carrying
value of the Back-end NIM residual.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company&#146;s exposure to credit losses related to its recourse securitization
activities is limited to the carrying value of its subordinated interests and
to the contractual limit of reimbursable losses under its corporate guarantees
less the recorded liability for such guarantees. These amounts are as follows:</font></p>

 <tr style="page-break-inside:avoid;">
  <td width="396" valign="bottom" style="padding:0pt .7pt 0pt 0pt;width:297.3pt;">
  <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:8.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COUNTRYWIDE FINANCIAL CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS&#151;(Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Note 31&#151;Commitments
and Contingencies<a name="Note31commitmentsAndContingencies_045616"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Legal Proceedings</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Countrywide and certain
subsidiaries are defendants in various legal proceedings involving matters
generally incidental to their businesses. Although it is difficult to predict
the resulting outcome of these proceedings, management believes, based on
discussions with counsel, that any resulting liability beyond those already recorded
will not materially affect the consolidated financial position of the Company.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Commitments to Buy or Sell Mortgage-Backed Securities
and Other Derivatives Contracts</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with its
open commitments to buy or sell MBS and other derivative contracts, the Company
may be required to maintain margin deposits. With respect to the MBS
commitments, these requirements are generally greatest during periods of
rapidly declining interest rates. With respect to other derivative contracts,
margin requirements are generally greatest during periods of increasing
interest rates. Margin deposits placed by the Company at December&nbsp;31,
2006, totaled $118.3 million.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Lease Commitments</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company leases office facilities under operating lease agreements extending through
July&nbsp;31, 2017. Future minimum annual rental commitments under these
non-cancelable operating leases with initial or remaining terms of one year or
more are as follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Rent expense was $231.2
million, $186.3 million and $160.7 million for the years ended December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2006,
2005 and 2004, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Restrictions on Transfers of Funds</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company and certain of
its subsidiaries are subject to regulatory and credit agreement restrictions
which limit the subsidiaries&#146; ability to transfer funds to the Company through
intercompany loans, advances or dividends. Pursuant to revolving credit
facilities existing at December&nbsp;31, 2006, the Company and CHL are required
to maintain a minimum consolidated net worth of $7.7 billion and $2.4&nbsp;billion,
respectively.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FHLB and FRB Stock</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Bank is required to
purchase stock in the FRB at an amount equal to 6% of its capital, one-half of
which must be paid currently with the balance due upon demand. The Bank is also
a member of the </font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-87</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COUNTRYWIDE FINANCIAL CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS&#151;(Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Federal
Home Loan Bank (&#147;FHLB&#148;) and, therefore, is required to purchase FHLB stock. For
the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, the Bank was required to purchase FHLB
stock at an amount equal to 0.2% of its assets up to a maximum of $25.0
million, plus 4.5% of total outstanding FHLB advances.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mortgage Reinsurance</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company provides
mortgage reinsurance on certain mortgage loans included in its servicing
portfolio through contracts with several primary mortgage insurance companies.
Under these agreements, the Company absorbs mortgage insurance losses in excess
of a specified percentage of the principal balance of a given pool of loans,
subject to a contractual limit, in exchange for a portion of the pools&#146;
mortgage insurance premiums. As of December&nbsp;31, 2006, approximately $90.0
billion of mortgage loans in the Company&#146;s servicing portfolio are covered by
such mortgage reinsurance contracts. Management believes it has adequate
valuation allowances in place to cover anticipated losses.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Securities Underwriting</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with the
Company&#146;s underwriting activities, the Company had commitments to purchase and
sell new issues of securities aggregating $3.5 billion and $3.2 billion,
respectively, at December&nbsp;31, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Note 32&#151;Loan
Commitments<a name="Note32loanCommitments_050855"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31,
2006 and 2005, the Company had undisbursed home equity lines of credit
commitments of $9.5 billion and $7.2 billion, respectively, as well as
undisbursed construction loan commitments of $3.5 billion and $1.5 billion,
respectively. As of December&nbsp;31, 2006, outstanding commitments to fund
mortgage loans totaled $35.5 billion.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Note 33&#151;Subsequent
Events<a name="Note33subsequentEvents_050857"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;30, 2007, the Company announced that
its Board of Directors declared a dividend of $0.15&nbsp;per common share
payable February&nbsp;28, 2007, to shareholders of record on February&nbsp;9,
2007.</font></p>
